question: After the readiness RFC is accepted, should OpenClaw core own these four named hosting profiles, runtime activation identity, and release-blocking packaged conformance as one v1 support contract?
rationale: The RFC creates durable core configuration, security-posture, support, and release-policy commitments; technical coherence alone cannot determine whether OpenClaw should own that product surface.

options.title: Defer behind readiness
options.body: Keep this RFC draft until https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/33 is accepted, then reassess the catalog and inspect refreshed package proof against the settled contract.

options.title: Accept the full contract
options.body: Approve all four profiles, activation identity, extension rules, and release-blocking packaged conformance as the initial core support promise.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Accept only the opt-in profile catalog and predicates while deferring activation identity and release-blocking conformance to follow-up RFCs.

recommendation.title: Defer behind readiness
recommendation.body: Keep this RFC draft until https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/33 is accepted, then reassess the catalog and inspect refreshed package proof against the settled contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available repository-member routing signal connected to adjacent profile-contract work; final ownership remains uncertain without a linked maintainer-discussion thread.
